question.problem:
Which of the following congruences have *precisely three* solutions modulo $21?$

I. $9x≡12\,(\text{mod}\,21)$

II. $6x≡15\,(\text{mod}\,21)$

III. $12x≡8\,(\text{mod}\,21)$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14269988/assets/b65fc4830e0b060d62226b41d5ccb7bdc63d0ad594f7a42a2628597409bba3af.png)

      

Recall the following facts regarding the congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n):$

- The congruence has no solutions modulo $n$ if and only if 

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)\,\text{⧸}|\,b.
$$

- The congruence has $\text{gcd}(a,n)$ solutions modulo $n$ if and only if 

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)\,|\,b.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our congruences.

- Congruence I has three solutions modulo $21.$ We have $a=9$ and $n=21$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(9,21)=3.
$$

Since $b=12$ is divisible by $3,$ this congruence has $3$ solutions.

- Congruence II has three solutions modulo $21.$ We have $a=6$ and $n=21$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(6,21)=3.
$$

Since $b=15$ is divisible by $3,$ this congruence has $3$ solutions.

- Congruence III has no solutions. We have $a=12$ and $n=21$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(12,21)=3.
$$

Since $b=8$ is not divisible by $3,$ this congruence has no solutions.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
